name: Dublin Airport
title: Dublin Airport guide: terminals, airlines and getting there
intro: Dublin has two terminals with separate security and drop-off points, and US flights clear immigration before they leave. Here's which airline uses which terminal.

terminals.name: Terminal 1
terminals.airlines: Ryanair and many other short-haul airlines
terminals.text: The older terminal, and the busier one in the early morning.

terminals.name: Terminal 2
terminals.airlines: Aer Lingus and most flights to the United States
terminals.text: Home to US preclearance, where you go through US immigration before you fly, so you land in the States as a domestic passenger. Allow extra time for it.

sections.heading: Getting to Dublin Airport
sections.text:
- **Bus:** there's no train. Dublin Express, Aircoach and Dublin Bus run from the city centre, about 30 to 45 minutes depending on traffic.
- **Car:** the airport is just off the M1 and M50. Each terminal has its own drop-off, so make sure your driver knows which one.

sections.heading: Moving between terminals
sections.text: Terminals 1 and 2 are a few minutes' walk apart, but they have separate security, so going to the wrong one costs you time on a busy morning.

faqs.question: Which terminal is Ryanair at Dublin Airport?
Which terminal is Aer Lingus at Dublin Airport?
What is US preclearance at Dublin Airport?
faqs.answer: You go through US immigration and customs in Dublin, in Terminal 2, before you fly, so you arrive in the US as a domestic passenger.
